Use cases/Lending & credit

Credit file review automation before underwriting

The agent pulls the bureau file, compares it with what the applicant declared, applies the flags in your policy and sends differences or adverse findings to an underwriter with the comparison laid out.

Book a demoSee how it runs

Works with

  • Custom REST
  • Credit bureau · via Custom REST
  • Loan origination system · via Custom REST

and any system with an API via Custom REST

What is a credit file review?

  • The procedure

    Before an underwriter decides, someone compares what the applicant declared with what the credit bureau reports. Undeclared obligations, thin histories and adverse entries all change the case. The review ends in a comparison and a list of flags for the underwriter to weigh.

  • What the agent does

    • Pulls the application from your loan origination system

    • Pulls the bureau file through Custom REST

    • Compares declared obligations with the ones the bureau reports

    • Applies the flags in your credit policy and saves the comparison

  • What your team decides

    • The credit decision

    • Any adverse action, with the reason recorded

    • Whether to ask the applicant about a difference

    • What other evidence a thin file needs

Setting up the Credit File Agent

Connect your systems

Read applications and bureau files from your systems through Custom REST, and keep each comparison and note in Google Drive.

  • Custom REST
  • Credit bureau · via Custom REST
  • Loan origination system · via Custom REST

Write the rules

The flags in your credit policy become CEL conditions. The agent reports what it found, and an underwriter makes any adverse decision.

Sample data
bureau.obligations.exists(o, !(o in declared.obligations))Ask an underwriter
bureau.history_months < policy.min_historyAsk an underwriter
flags.size() == 0Check passed

The underwriter sees the application and the bureau file side by side, with the difference marked, and the decision is logged.

Start it from the event

A new application in your loan origination system starts the check by webhook, and a refreshed bureau file starts another. A daily schedule lists files still waiting on a decision.

  • Inbound webhook · application received
  • Daily at 06:00 · files awaiting a decision
  • Inbound webhook · bureau file refreshed

Version and evaluate

Test each version on a consistent file, an undeclared obligation and a thin file. When your credit policy changes, the new flags are checked against those cases before publishing.

Questions about credit file review automation

What does the underwriter see?

The application and the bureau file side by side, with each difference and flag marked, plus the rule that raised it.

How are thin files handled?

Your policy sets the minimum history. A file below it goes to an underwriter, who can ask for other evidence, such as bank statements in the example.

Can a refreshed bureau file restart the check?

Yes. A webhook from your bureau or origination system starts a new check when the file is refreshed.

Which systems does it connect to?

Your loan origination system and credit bureau through Custom REST, and Google Drive for comparisons and notes.

    Each entry carries the hash of the one before it. Verifying the log recomputes the chain and flags entries that no longer match.
